passage: The canteen was loud, the bell was in five minutes, and Sachin was in a rush. "So you're saying you don't want to be group leader? Why not? What's the reason?" he fired at Chandrika. She stiffened and looked at her tray. "I never said that." Sachin realised his voice was sharp. He put his fork down. "Sorry. That sounded like an interrogation. I really want to understand. Do you want to talk at break, when it's quieter?" Chandrika's shoulders lowered. "Yes. I'm not sure myself yet." "Take your time," said Sachin. "I'll wait."

qa.q: How many minutes were left before the bell?
qa.a: The bell was in five minutes.

qa.q: What was Chandrika feeling when Sachin fired his questions?
qa.a: She felt pressured and defensive, since she stiffened and looked at her tray. She also said she wasn't sure herself.

qa.q: What could Sachin do differently next time?
qa.a: He can slow down, use a warmer tone and pick a quieter moment. Probing questions can feel like interrogation when rushed.

qa.q: How might Sachin have seen his own questions?
qa.a: He wanted to understand, but noticed his voice was sharp. He apologised and offered a quieter time.

grounding: A teenager asks confirming and probing questions that feel like interrogation, and softens his tone.

passage: After Imran missed the match, Parveen sat next to him on the wall. "So you're saying you're fine with sitting out? What's behind that?" she asked, warmly, her head tilted. Imran picked at his laces. "My knee felt off. And I didn't want to say." It felt good to be asked. The next day, a senior stopped him in the corridor and said the same thing in a hard voice: "So you're saying you're fine with sitting out? Reason?" Imran felt himself go tense and defensive. The words were nearly the same, but they landed differently.

qa.q: Where did Parveen sit next to Imran?
qa.a: She sat next to him on the wall.

qa.q: What was Imran feeling when the senior asked him the same question?
qa.a: He felt tense and defensive, since the hard voice made it feel like an interrogation. With Parveen's warmth he felt supported.

qa.q: What could the senior do to make his question feel supportive?
qa.a: Use a warmer tone and show he's on Imran's side. Probing questions depend on tone and relationship.

qa.q: How might Parveen see her questions compared to the senior's?
qa.a: Parveen asked warmly as a friend and it helped him open up. The same words in a hard voice from someone less close can feel like pressure.

grounding: A teenager's confirming and probing questions feel supportive from a friend and like interrogation from a harder voice.
